term: incorruptible simply (incorruptibile simpliciter); sempiternal in In Metaph. IX, lect. 9
definition: `IncorruptibleSimply CanFailToBe esse x`: x cannot fail to be in substance, the respect `esse` (simpliciter est corruptibile, quod potest non esse secundum substantiam, In Metaph. IX, lect. 9 n. 4). Aquinas passes in the same lecture between 'sempiternal' (n. 1, n. 6) and 'incorruptible simply' (n. 5); both are read as this predicate. It is not the timeless eternity of DEF-ETERNAL, and it allows potency in a respect other than substance (n. 6).
